findings_addressed: FIX-5 [P2] 1/1 — OVER-SPECIFIC CLI ORACLE FOR THE UNTIERED-MANIFEST ERROR (scripts/sbom-survey/tests/test_cli.py, AC-SBOM-21). THIS FINDING IS THE INVERSE OF THE CLASS THE PREVIOUS FOUR ROUNDS FIXED. Every one of the ten earlier findings was a test too PERMISSIVE — it would let a wrong implementation pass. This one is too STRICT: it would REJECT A CORRECT IMPLEMENTATION. The criterion drives the CLI with a tier map whose single rule excludes dev/release/fixtures/ and therefore covers NO real manifest, and REQ-4 then requires only that the CLI NAME THE OFFENDING PATH on stderr. The assertion was `assert "Cargo.toml" in proc.stderr`, which accepts exactly one basename. A Slice-32 implementation that walks discovered paths in `git ls-files` order legitimately fails FIRST on Cargo.lock — or on any other tracked manifest, since the order in which the tool reaches an untiered path is an implementation choice REQ-4 does not constrain — names that path, satisfies REQ-4 in full, and STILL FAILS THIS TEST. CLOSED by asserting that stderr names SOME MEMBER OF THE SET of currently-untiered tracked manifests: the 21 tracked manifest paths that lie outside dev/release/fixtures/ (29 tracked manifests minus the 8 skew fixtures the one rule excludes), DERIVED FROM GIT through the suite's existing conftest.tracked_manifest_paths() helper rather than written as a second literal list — a hand-maintained list is exactly what drifted in rounds 1-3 (the missing setup.cfg, the stale 28). A VACUITY GUARD fails the criterion if that set is ever empty, since a tier map that happened to cover the whole repository would leave the assertion grading nothing. The failure message prints the full expected set alongside the actual stderr, so a Slice-32 implementer sees immediately what would have satisfied it.

FIX-5 — AC-SBOM-07 CHECKED FOR THE SAME DEFECT AND DOES NOT HAVE IT. The round-5 steer asked whether the sibling unit-level criterion (test_tiering.py::test_untiered_manifest_raises_untiered_manifest_error, which asserts UntieredManifestError names the path) carries the same over-specificity. It does not, and the reason is structural rather than incidental: TierMap.classify() is handed EXACTLY ONE path by the test ('some/brand/new/Cargo.toml'), so the error it raises can only be about THAT path — there is no discovery order, no set of candidates and no choice of victim, which means naming it is the SOLE correct behaviour and asserting it rejects nothing correct. The over-specificity is only possible where THE TOOL PICKS THE PATH ITSELF, which in this suite is the CLI alone. No change was made to AC-SBOM-07, and design §5.3 now states the distinction so it is not re-litigated.

FIX-5 COUNT — N DID NOT MOVE. This is an assertion correction inside an existing criterion, not a new one: still 23 criteria, 23 tests, 23 failures, 0 passed, 0 skipped, 0 errors. No id minted, none retired, and no statement of the number was touched — design §4 header and table, design §8 gate 6, scripts/sbom-survey/README.md, dev/DOC-INDEX.md and this JSON all still read 23. The last count move remains fix-3's 22 -> 23 (§12).

FIX-5 SCOPE — DELIBERATELY MINIMAL, AT THE ROUND CAP. Two files changed, 60 insertions / 8 deletions. No sweep, no refactor, no strengthening of unrelated assertions, no restructuring: the next review is round 5's successor at a hard budget that halts at round 6, and a broad diff now would open new surface and cost the slice its close. The only extension of scope taken was the one the steer permitted — checking AC-SBOM-07 for the same defect (it does not have it).

FIX-4 [P2] 1/2 (round 4, STILL CLOSED) — THE INJECTED PUBLISHED-SOURCE WAS NEVER EXERCISED THROUGH run_survey (test_registry.py, AC-SBOM-17). The criterion called classify_status() DIRECTLY, so Slice 32 could ship a correct comparator while run_survey(..., published=...) never called published.latest() and left every staleness row 'unknown' — and AC-SBOM-15/16 would still pass, because both inject a source that legitimately yields 'unknown' for everything. CLOSED by a second leg that drives a POSITIVE StaticSource THROUGH run_survey and asserts on the resulting staleness rows: 'current', 'outdated' and 'ahead' must all appear, each carrying the INJECTED latest_version, while every package absent from the mapping stays 'unknown' / None (which is what stops a blanket fill). Probes are taken from a preceding offline run rather than hardcoded, and constrained to a unique (ecosystem, name) and a plain major.minor.patch with major >= 1 so both sentinels (9999.0.0, 0.0.1) order unambiguously under BOTH comparators. Design §5.4 carries the probe table.

FIX-4 [P3] 2/2 (round 4, STILL CLOSED) — THE --describe TIER VOCABULARY WAS NOT ASSERTED (test_cli.py, AC-SBOM-19). §5.9 requires --describe to publish the vocabulary, but the assertions passed if the command omitted `tiers` entirely or returned wrong values. CLOSED by asserting `tiers` is PRESENT and that tuple(described['tiers']) == ('shipped', 'dev-tooling', 'eval-only') in that ruled order, with the order now stated in §5.9 so test and spec cannot drift.

FIX-4 SWEEP (round 4, STILL CLOSED) — all 23 criteria were swept for the class 'a criterion is graded against a helper while the integration boundary that must call it goes ungraded', which had appeared in three separate rounds.
